The source requests restoration of the existing elevation hierarchy rather than changing it; the proposed updates primarily introduce terminal-language semantics owned by a separate Requirement.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Hi Marisol,

All three foundational rules have now been restored and verified in the finalized alignment study.

Across the locked Option 2 (Balanced Flow) kerning and Satin Reflection finish, the three reference lines clearly establish the required mathematical relationships:

Line 1 (Cap Height): This defines the standard cap height across the E’s and L’s, making the second V’s quiet extension above the main letterforms visible.

Line 2 (Second V Height +2%): This confirms that the second V’s +2% increase is calculated strictly from its own individual height, preserving it as a subtle, restrained echo.

Line 3 (Hero V & É Accent Peak): Passing through both the Hero V right-arm peak and the É accent peak, this guide confirms their 1:1 horizontal alignment and shared master geometry.

Together, the guides show how cohesive, deliberate, and balanced the full identity has become. I’m excited to hear your thoughts as we lock it in.

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer reports restoring the shared endpoint hierarchy, including the second V’s proportional elevation and exact Hero V/É accent peak alignment.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Hi Marisol,

The reset call gave the file exactly the correction it needed. I’ve now delivered a clean, distraction-free presentation devoted entirely to restoring the foundation and the system hierarchy.

The Hero V Foundation: Its locked master geometry, slope, and proportion have been strictly reinstated. The terminal is a straight architectural shear with subtly softened corners; it remains completely linear, without any calligraphic sweep or curve.

The É Accent: This element directly inherits the Hero V’s master terminal geometry and aligns cleanly with it at peak height.

The Second V: Calculated at +2% strictly relative to its own individual height, it functions as a quiet, understated echo that remains subordinate to the Hero V.

This restored baseline returns us to the core structural rules we established while retaining the intended quiet elevation. I look forward to hearing your thoughts.

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer reports restoring the endpoint hierarchy after the prior failure, including Hero V/É peak alignment and the second V’s proportional elevation.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Kenji,

Having reviewed the latest presentation, I have decided that the project will end here. Despite the explicit instructions, none of these examples preserve the locked hierarchy and geometry previously established for the Hero V and second V.

Continuing would mean reopening and reconstructing decisions that were already resolved, and I do not consider another revision cycle a good use of either your time or mine. Please make no additional design revisions.

Instead, send me every editable working file produced during the project in its current state. The handoff must include the original vector/source files, all presentation boards, and the exported artwork.

I appreciate the time and effort you invested in the project and wish you the best going forward.

Marisol

execution.observed_behavior: The client reports that the latest terminal-exploration examples again failed to preserve the locked Hero V and second V endpoint hierarchy and geometry.
